rule_applied: Cruzes & Dyba (2015) section 6 transferability - scope-boundary documentation; Petersen 2015 section 6 (threats to validity - construct boundary)
rationale: Post-fix cross-model spot-check (64-paper stratified sample, GPT-5.4 verifier against Gemini 3.1 Pro extractor) surfaced nine residual B4 (f3_population) disagreements AFTER the A5/B4 prompt patch had cut A5 fails by 92% (24-to-2) and B4 fails by 68% (28-to-9). Manual review of the nine verifier rationales shows the residual disagreements are NOT extraction errors in the Gemini coding given the current F3 vocabulary - they are boundary cases where the paper studies a non-developer end-user population that is not represented in VALID_F3_POP: creative writers, older adults using feeding robots, accessibility QA testers, mixed developer/practitioner cohorts. Our F3 vocabulary (Professional SWE, Student, Citizen Developer, OSS Contributor, Mixed, N/A) is derived from the proposal 3.4 codebook whose scope is software-engineering practitioners; it deliberately does not carry an End-user category. Three options considered: (a) extend VALID_F3_POP to add End-user and re-extract the 9 papers (~2 USD, +10min); (b) accept the scope boundary, log it as a transferability limitation, document the 9 papers here (deadline-preserving); (c) mark the 9 papers as out-of-scope (EC3). Option (b) selected: the 9 papers studied valid human-AI-for-SE interactions by non-developer populations (accessibility QA, mixed cohorts, end-user studies of SE-adjacent tooling) and do belong in the corpus per IC1-IC3; expanding F3 mid-study would destabilise upstream F1/F2 calibration. The scope boundary is explicitly named in Phase 6 of the manuscript and the nine affected papers can be re-classified in ERP3 if taxonomy evolution becomes appropriate. No data is deleted; F3 values stay as Gemini assigned them under the current codebook.

rule_applied: Cruzes & Dyba (2015) section 6 dependability - prompt-level defect correction without destabilising re-extraction
rationale: Post-fix spot-check (consolidated 63 papers, 1827 checks) found 14 A6 (sample_description captures who was studied) fails traceable to over-aggressive wording in rule 9 of extraction.py build_system_prompt. Rule 9 originally instructed the extractor to set sample_description to null when the study has no human participants. The verifier correctly flagged this: dataset/benchmark studies still have a sample (e.g. 100 Android apps, 587 patch reviews) and that information is valuable for RQ1 landscape work. Rule 9 wording patched to: set sample_size to null, but sample_description should describe the artefact sample. extraction_schema.md sample_description row updated correspondingly. No re-extraction performed because: (a) A5 sample_size values are correct (the RQ1-critical field), (b) no Phase 4/5 downstream consumer keys on sample_description for filtering or stratification, (c) cost of re-running 640-paper extraction (~USD 15.50 + half day) not justified given modest improvement on a non-critical field, (d) keeps extraction history clean (one v1 pre-fix + one v2 post-fix versus three versions). Patch preserved for reproducibility and any future re-extraction.

rule_applied: Cruzes & Dyba (2011) Step 3 - bidirectional trace preserved; CLAUDE.md append-only decision register (corrections as new rows)
rationale: Task 4.1 --verify flagged two pass-1 descriptive codes ('Generating code and docs', 'PHP Code Generation') as missing from consolidated_codes.csv. Root-cause trace in .consolidate_state.json: cluster 59 was originally labelled 'Automated Software Asset Synthesis' and held the two codes; rater pressed [s]plit, spawning singletons; those singletons were re-split in a chain and the terminal singletons (727, 728) were then [m]erged back into cluster 59. _merge_into copied the members into 59's members list, but emit_consolidated skips clusters whose status is 'split' or 'merged', so the two codes were silently orphaned at emit time. Recovery: cluster 59 flipped from status='split' to status='approved' in .consolidate_state.json; members deduplicated to the two distinct codes; member_passage_map deduplicated from 4 to 2 unique tuples; final_label set to the pre-existing proposed_label 'Automated Software Asset Synthesis'; confirmed_by='AT-recovery'; notes stamped with audit trail. consolidated_codes.csv re-emitted via --resume (_finalize_if_complete); --verify now passes. Root-cause patch applied in code/coding_consolidate.py: [m]erge-into action now rejects targets whose status is 'split' or 'merged' (prevents data loss at emit). Backups: artifacts/synthesis/.consolidate_state.json.bak-before-c59-recovery and consolidated_codes.csv.bak-before-c59-recovery.
